title: Hard Hat Inspection Checklist (OSHA 29 CFR 1926.100)
subtitle: For site supervisors checking helmet use and helmet criteria in any area with head-injury hazards.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For any Defect, record what you found and correct it before the employee works in the hazard area.
The helmet manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks, such as helmet condition; follow them as well.

sections.title: Head-injury hazards and helmet use
items: Areas where a worker's head could be injured by impact are identified for the shift.
Areas where objects could fall onto workers' heads are identified.
Areas where objects could be propelled toward workers' heads are identified.
Areas where employees face electric shock or burn hazards to the head are identified.
Every employee in an identified area is wearing a protective helmet.

sections.title: Helmet criteria
items: Each employee has been provided with head protection by the employer.
Helmet label or documentation shows ANSI Z89.1-2009 (mark N/A if another listed edition applies).
Marking or maker's data confirms ANSI Z89.1-2003 (mark N/A if another listed edition applies).
Manufacturer's records confirm ANSI Z89.1-1997 (mark N/A if another listed edition applies).
Every helmet in use matches at least one of the three listed editions or has an equivalence record (section D).

sections.title: High-voltage exposure
items: Employees exposed to high-voltage shock and burn hazards are listed by name or task.
Their helmets meet Section 9.7 (Electrical Insulation) of ANSI Z89.1-2009, -2003 or -1997, as shown on the label or maker's documentation.
No employee exposed to high-voltage hazards wears a helmet lacking the Section 9.7 insulation specification.

sections.title: Alternative helmets
items: Any helmet not built to a listed ANSI Z89.1 edition is identified by type and wearer.
The employer can demonstrate the helmet is equally or more effective than one built to a (b)(1) edition.
The equivalence evidence can be produced on site or on request.

references: 29 CFR 1926.100: Head protection (Part 1926 Subpart E: Personal Protective and Life Saving Equipment)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
